description: The internals of database engines at graduate depth: storage layout, indexes, query execution and optimisation, concurrency control, recovery, distribution, column stores and the NoSQL and NewSQL landscape. Students read query plans, simulate transactions and index structures, build small engine components and finish with a benchmarked research-style project.
modelledOn: Garcia-Molina, Ullman and Widom, Database Systems: The Complete Book
Hellerstein, Stonebraker and Hamilton, Architecture of a Database System
outcomes: Estimate the I/O cost of scans, index lookups and join algorithms and predict which one an optimiser will pick.
Implement and analyse B+ tree and LSM-tree operations, including node splits, compaction and write amplification.
Decide serialisability of schedules and explain how two-phase locking, timestamps and snapshot isolation prevent or permit anomalies.
Trace write-ahead logging and ARIES recovery through a crash and show the state of the database after each phase.
Compare partitioning, replication and distributed commit designs and state what each guarantees under failure.
Design, run and critically report a benchmark that compares two storage or execution designs.

units.title: DBMS architecture and storage management
topics: Layers of a DBMS: parser, optimiser, executor, access methods, buffer manager, storage and log manager
Pages, slotted-page layout, record formats and free-space management
Buffer pool replacement: LRU, clock, LRU-K and scan-resistant policies; sequential flooding
Row, column and hybrid (PAX) layouts; the disk and SSD I/O cost model

units.title: Indexing structures
topics: B+ trees: search, insertion with splits, deletion with merges, bulk loading and latch crabbing
Hash indexes: static, extendible and linear hashing
Log-structured merge trees: memtable, sorted runs, compaction strategies and write amplification
Bitmap indexes, Bloom filters and R-trees for spatial data
Index selection: clustered, covering, partial and composite indexes and the cost of maintenance

units.title: Query execution
topics: Iterator (Volcano), vectorised and compiled execution models
External merge sort and its I/O cost
Join algorithms: block nested loop, index nested loop, sort-merge and grace hash join, with cost formulae
Aggregation, duplicate elimination and set operators
Pipelining versus materialisation, and intra-query parallelism

units.title: Query optimisation
topics: Relational algebra equivalences, predicate and projection pushdown, and rule-based rewriting
Statistics: histograms, distinct counts, selectivity and cardinality estimation errors
Plan enumeration: System R dynamic programming, left-deep trees and interesting orders
Transformation-based optimisers: Cascades, memo structures and top-down search
Reading EXPLAIN output, hints, plan regressions and adaptive query processing

units.title: Transactions and concurrency control
topics: ACID, schedules, conflict serialisability and precedence graphs
Two-phase locking, strict 2PL, deadlock detection and prevention, and multigranularity locking
Timestamp ordering and optimistic concurrency control
Multiversion concurrency control, snapshot isolation, write skew and serialisable snapshot isolation
SQL isolation levels and anomalies: dirty read, lost update, non-repeatable read and phantom

units.title: Recovery and logging
topics: Steal and no-force buffer policies; the write-ahead logging rule
ARIES: analysis, redo and undo passes, compensation log records and fuzzy checkpoints
Shadow paging, copy-on-write and log-structured storage compared with update-in-place
Group commit, fsync cost and durability on SSDs and cloud disks
Backup, archive logs and point-in-time recovery

units.title: Distributed and replicated databases
topics: Partitioning: hash, range and consistent hashing; rebalancing and hot spots
Replication: leader-follower, multi-leader, quorum, and replication lag anomalies
Atomic commit: two-phase commit, its blocking problem and three-phase commit
Consensus for replicated logs: Paxos and Raft, leader election and log replication
Distributed transactions and globally consistent databases using synchronised clocks
Distributed query processing: shuffle, broadcast and co-located joins

units.title: Column stores, in-memory systems and NoSQL
topics: Column stores: compression (run-length, dictionary, bit-packing), late materialisation and zone maps
Vectorised execution with SIMD and in-memory databases: logging, snapshots and cache efficiency
NoSQL families (key-value, document, wide-column, graph) and BASE trade-offs
NewSQL and HTAP systems: distributed SQL with transactions, and mixed workloads
Choosing a data system: workload analysis and the TPC-C, TPC-H and YCSB benchmarks

units.title: Research methods and project
topics: Reading and critiquing a systems paper: claim, mechanism, evaluation and threats
Benchmark design: workloads, warm-up, throughput, latency percentiles and confidence intervals
Open problems: learned indexes, learned cardinality estimation and serverless databases
Project: implement and evaluate a storage or query-engine component and report the results

schedule.title: Engine architecture and pages
schedule.exercise: Draw the layers of a DBMS and trace a SELECT through them, then lay out ten variable-length records in a slotted page and update one so it grows.

tasks.title: Insert, delete and grow variable-length records in a slotted page, and record the slot directory and free space after each of eight operations
Run a query with EXPLAIN on a three-table schema and label which component produced each part of the plan and which stages ran before execution
Implement a slotted page with insert, delete and compaction, and test on 1,000 random operations that all live records remain readable

schedule.title: Buffer management and layouts
schedule.exercise: Simulate LRU, clock and LRU-K on a trace that mixes a hot set with a large sequential scan, and count the hits for each.

tasks.title: Replay a page-reference trace of 40 requests through LRU and clock with a 4-frame pool and count hits and misses for each
Generate a trace where a large scan follows a hot working set, run LRU and LRU-K, and show how sequential flooding hurts LRU hit rate
Compute the I/O cost of scanning a 1 GB table in row and column layout when a query reads 2 of 20 columns, on HDD and SSD parameters

schedule.title: B+ trees, hashing and LSM trees
schedule.exercise: Build a B+ tree of order 4 from 20 keys showing every split, then compare a B+ tree with an LSM tree for a write-heavy workload.

tasks.title: Insert 20 keys into a B+ tree of order 4, step through each node split, then delete five keys and show merges and redistributions
Implement an LSM tree with a memtable, flushing and size-tiered compaction, and measure write amplification over 100,000 inserts and updates
Create composite, covering and partial indexes for a query set on a 100,000-row table and compare the plans and write costs of each choice

schedule.title: Operators and join algorithms
schedule.exercise: Compute the I/O cost of block nested loop, sort-merge and grace hash join for two relations of 1,000 and 200 pages with 50 buffer pages.

tasks.title: Compute the I/O cost of external merge sort for 10,000 pages with 100 buffer pages and plot the number of passes against buffer size
Force a nested-loop, merge and hash join on the same query by changing settings, and compare estimated cost, actual time and rows examined
Implement iterator-style scan, filter and hash-join operators, compose them into a plan, and compare their speed with a vectorised version on 1 million rows

schedule.title: Equivalences, statistics and plan search
schedule.exercise: Rewrite a five-table query using algebra equivalences, estimate selectivities from a histogram, and enumerate the left-deep plans System R would keep.

tasks.title: Rewrite a query by pushing selections below joins by hand, then compare its plan with the optimiser output and explain any difference
Build a skewed table, compare the optimiser row estimates with actual rows for five predicates, and refresh statistics to see the estimates improve
Implement System R dynamic programming for join ordering on five relations with given cardinalities and verify against brute-force enumeration of all orders

schedule.title: Cascades, plans and regressions
schedule.exercise: Given two EXPLAIN outputs before and after a statistics change, diagnose why the plan regressed and propose a fix with evidence.

tasks.title: Read three EXPLAIN ANALYZE outputs, mark the node with the largest estimation error and the node that dominates time, and explain each
Step through a memo-based search over join orders for three tables, recording the groups, the best expression per group and the pruned alternatives
Diagnose a slow query with a bad cardinality estimate, apply three fixes (statistics, index, rewrite) and report the speed-up each gives

schedule.title: Serialisability and locking
schedule.exercise: Draw the precedence graph for four schedules, decide which are conflict serialisable, and trace strict 2PL on the one that deadlocks.

tasks.title: Check six schedules for conflict serialisability by building the precedence graph and giving an equivalent serial order for each that passes
Run two interleaved transactions that update accounts in opposite order, produce a deadlock, and record the victim chosen and the lock waits
Implement optimistic concurrency with validation, run 1,000 transactions at low and high conflict rates, and compare abort rates with a locking scheme

schedule.title: MVCC, snapshot isolation and anomalies
schedule.exercise: Construct write skew on a two-doctor on-call rota under snapshot isolation, and show how a serialisable level or a locking read prevents it.

tasks.title: Reproduce dirty read, lost update, non-repeatable read and phantom at each isolation level and fill a table of which anomalies each level allows
Demonstrate write skew with two sessions under snapshot isolation, then prevent it using serialisable mode and report the transaction that is aborted
Implement a small multiversion store with snapshot reads and first-committer-wins, and test it with a workload that checks no lost update occurs

schedule.title: Write-ahead logging and ARIES
schedule.exercise: Run ARIES recovery on a given log with a crash after a checkpoint, writing the analysis tables and the redo and undo actions.

tasks.title: Step through ARIES analysis, redo and undo on a 15-record log, tracking the dirty page table, transaction table and compensation records written
Run committed and uncommitted updates, kill the engine mid-transaction, restart, and verify that only committed changes survive and explain by the log
Measure commit throughput with fsync on every commit and with group commit across 1,000 transactions, and explain the gain and the durability risk

schedule.title: Partitioning, replication and commit
schedule.exercise: Design the partitioning and replication of a national ID database across three data centres and state what happens when one is lost.

tasks.title: Implement consistent hashing with virtual nodes, add and remove a node, and count how many of 10,000 keys move compared with modulo hashing
Step through two-phase commit with a coordinator crash after the prepare phase and show which participants are blocked and why
Set up a leader and two followers, create replica lag, and show a read-your-writes violation and a way to avoid it in routing

schedule.title: Consensus and distributed queries
schedule.exercise: Trace Raft leader election and log replication through a leader failure, then plan a distributed join on a table partitioned by region.

tasks.title: Run Raft with five nodes, kill the leader during replication, and record the election, term change and which entries were committed or lost
Plan a join of an orders table partitioned by region with a small product table and compare broadcast and shuffle by bytes moved
Evaluate a case for a globally distributed database for a pan-African bank, weighing consistency, latency, clock assumptions and regulation, and recommend a design

schedule.title: Column stores, in-memory and NewSQL
schedule.exercise: Choose among a row store, a column store, a key-value store and a NewSQL system for four workloads, justified with measured numbers.

tasks.title: Apply run-length and dictionary encoding to a sorted column of 1 million values and compare space and scan speed with the raw column
Run an analytical query on a row-oriented and a column-oriented layout of the same data and explain the time difference from the plans
Run a YCSB-style workload with 95 percent reads and one with 50 percent writes on two stores, and compare throughput and 99th-percentile latency

schedule.title: Research project and benchmark report
schedule.exercise: Present the project: hypothesis, implementation, benchmark design, results with confidence intervals, and a critical discussion of threats to validity.

tasks.title: Critique a systems paper from the reading list by rewriting its claim, listing the experiments that support it, and naming three threats to validity
Design a benchmark with warm-up, ten repetitions and percentile reporting for an index lookup, and compute means and 95 percent confidence intervals
Implement and evaluate a storage or query component (for example a buffer policy, join operator or compaction rule) against a baseline and report results
